subject: Go-live certification: VPC + on-prem smoke acceptance for AcmeCloud
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: david.roberts@acmecloud.com, infra-team@acmecloud.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Go-live certification: VPC + on-prem smoke acceptance for AcmeCloud

Hi David / Acme infra,

We have the final go/no-go checklist in place for the VPC + on-prem deployment scheduled for this coming maintenance window (May 3 23:00-02:00 UTC). Please find the final runbook attached (RI-Runbook-v1.4.pdf). Key asks for today:

- Confirm that your on-prem firewall team has applied the ACLs in network-acl-final.txt and that peering is in the established state.
- Confirm the maintenance window (same as above) and who will be the pager for external network issues.
- Please provide the last-minute contact for procurement/ops for any DocuSign/contract signoff.

Marissa will run the smoke checklist during the window and will post the CSV results. Karthik will be on the network bridge. Soojin will own telemetry validation and tracing. Mateo will run the DB migration verification playback if needed.

If we get green on the preflight by 15:00 PT today, we will consider this certified for go-live and proceed with the cutover according to step 2 of the runbook.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Program Manager, Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RI-Runbook-v1.4.pdf (runbook), network-acl-final.txt (ACL diff)
From: David Roberts <david.roberts@acmecloud.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: infra-team@acmecloud.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Go-live certification: VPC + on-prem smoke acceptance for AcmeCloud

Rachel,

Thanks — confirming the maintenance window and our side.

- ACLs: Applied in staging and pre-prod earlier this morning; firewall team will apply identical ACLs to on-prem edge at T-60. I have asked Katie Yang to be the primary pager (katie.yang@acmecloud.com).
- Peering: BGP session established with the Redwood test peer; we will promote to production at T-30.
- DocuSign: procurement has the signoff ready; I will send the envelope once we hit green.

I will be on the bridge for the window and will report any external network flaps immediately.

—David
David Roberts
Head of Cloud Engineering, AcmeCloud

Quick update from the runbook playback I ran against the staging cluster this morning:

- Step 1 (DNS & Peering): OK — records TTL lowered, peering validated.
- Step 2 (Ingress ACLs): Matched expected rules; two ephemeral deny entries in staging were removed.
- Step 3 (KV cache warmup): Warmup took ~18s for a 16k token prefix distribution (expected <25s).
- Step 4 (Telemetry hooks): Sampling looks good; traces are flowing to the observability endpoint.

I attached the smoke-results-20270502.csv with the run outputs and the short checklist as comments.

Action items for the window:
- Karthik to validate BGP advertise communities and ensure graceful restart is enabled.
- Soojin to verify span sampling targets and alert thresholds post-cutover.
- Mateo to standby for the DB schema checksum step.

If we don't see anything surprising in the preflight at 15:00 PT, give me the go and I'll run the step-by-step acceptance during the window.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: smoke-results-20270502.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rachel.kim@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: david.roberts@acmecloud.com, mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Go-live certification: VPC + on-prem smoke acceptance for AcmeCloud

Thanks — quick network confirmation:

- BGP: graceful-restart enabled on both peers; keepalive timers adjusted to match Acme's recommendation (60s).
- Communities: We will advertise only the production prefixes (no broad aggregates).
- MTU: Verified end-to-end 9000 bytes for RDMA paths; fallback route will use 1500 for non-RDMA.
- ACL logging: Enabled but rate-limited to prevent telemetry storms.

I'll join the bridge at T-30 and run the BGP withdraw/announce test at T+20mins into the window. If anything deviates we will roll back to the pre-cutover peering state (runbook rollback step 4b).

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Network Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Go-live certification: VPC + on-prem smoke acceptance for AcmeCloud — ACCEPTED

Team / Acme,

Post-cutover summary and sign-off: we executed the cutover during the agreed window and completed the acceptance tests from the runbook. Highlights below — full CSV and logs attached.

- Network & Peering: BGP flaps observed at T+8m but recovered automatically; graceful-restart held and no production traffic loss.
- ACLs: No unexpected denies seen; one deny was rate-limited and traced to a legacy monitoring IP (blocked, then whitelisted per runbook).
- App-level smoke: 98% success rate on the canonical generate/chat endpoints for 30m post-cutover; latency delta within SLA (<15% over baseline).
- Telemetry & Traces: Sampling and shards verified. No missing spans.
- DB migration checksum: Verified match on schema and row counts.

Actions and follow-ups:
- David/Katie: confirm procurement will close the DocuSign envelope (link above).
- SRE: continue enhanced telemetry for 72 hours; Soojin to create the short-lived alert dashboard.
- Network: Karthik to publish final BGP session stats and the MTU verification report.

Acceptance: AcmeCloud + Redwood sign-off for go-live is documented here. This thread serves as the official acceptance record for the deployment.

Thanks everyone for the fast coordination.

Rachel Kim
Senior Program Manager, Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: smoke-results-20270502.csv, network-acl-final.txt
